find_container_images.description: Find the public container images that share a given OCI layer chain id, with each one's registry, pull count and whether it is an official image. Take a chain id from a local image and this traces it back to what it was built from.
find_container_images.name: find_container_images

parameters.description: The OCI chain id of the layer stack to match, including its 'sha256:' prefix.
parameters.name: chain_id

parameters.description: How many rows to return. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

find_similarly_named_packages.description: List the packages whose names look like this one's - the typosquat check. Run it over what a project actually installs to surface the near-miss names an attacker would publish, or over a name before you depend on it to find the popular package it is imitating.
find_similarly_named_packages.name: find_similarly_named_packages

parameters.description: The registry the package is published to.
parameters.name: system

parameters.description: The package's name exactly as its registry spells it. Maven uses 'group:artifact' and Go uses the full module path.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: How many rows to return. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

find_versions_by_hash.description: Find which published package versions a file belongs to, from its checksum alone - the way to identify an unlabelled jar, wheel or tarball, or to confirm that a vendored file really is the release it claims to be. Paste the digest as hex (what sha256sum prints) or as base64; both work.
find_versions_by_hash.display_name: Identify a file by its hash
find_versions_by_hash.name: find_versions_by_hash

parameters.description: The algorithm the digest was produced with.
parameters.name: hash_type

parameters.description: The file's digest, in hex or base64. A hex digest is converted for you.
parameters.name: hash_value

parameters.description: Optional. Narrow the search to one registry when you already know which it is.
parameters.name: system

parameters.description: Optional. Narrow the search to one package, to confirm a file is the release you expect.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: Optional. Narrow the search to one version.
parameters.name: version

parameters.description: How many rows to return. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

get_advisory.description: Get one security advisory by its OSV id - a GHSA, a GO, a PYSEC or a RUSTSEC identifier - with its title, its CVE aliases, and its CVSS v3 score, vector and severity rating. The ids come back on every version this integration returns.

advisory.title: express vulnerable to XSS via response.redirect()

get_advisory.name: get_advisory

parameters.description: The advisory's OSV identifier, as it appears in a version's advisory list.
parameters.name: advisory_id

get_dependencies.description: Get the full dependency graph a version actually resolves to, with every transitive package pinned to a concrete version - the answer to 'what would installing this pull in?'. Narrow it to direct or transitive dependencies, and read the edges to see which package asked for which.
get_dependencies.name: get_dependencies

parameters.description: The registry the package is published to.
parameters.name: system

parameters.description: The package's name exactly as its registry spells it. Maven uses 'group:artifact' and Go uses the full module path.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: The version to look at. Leave empty to use the registry's current default (latest) version.
parameters.name: version

parameters.description: Whether to return the whole graph, only the packages this version asks for itself, or only the ones pulled in through those. Defaults to all.
parameters.name: relation

parameters.description: How many rows to return. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

get_dependents.description: Count how many public packages depend on a version, split into the ones that name it directly and the ones that reach it through something else. The measure of how much would break if this package broke.
get_dependents.name: get_dependents

parameters.description: The registry the package is published to.
parameters.name: system

parameters.description: The package's name exactly as its registry spells it. Maven uses 'group:artifact' and Go uses the full module path.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: The version to look at. Leave empty to use the registry's current default (latest) version.
parameters.name: version

get_findings.description: Check a package or one of its versions for the things that should stop you depending on it: known malicious code, deprecation, known vulnerabilities, very low usage, and a release still inside its cooldown window. Each finding carries a risk level, and deps.dev names the versions it would recommend instead.
get_findings.name: get_findings

parameters.description: The registry the package is published to.
parameters.name: system

parameters.description: The package's name exactly as its registry spells it. Maven uses 'group:artifact' and Go uses the full module path.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: The version to look at. Leave empty to use the registry's current default (latest) version.
parameters.name: version

get_findings_batch.description: Run the safety check over as many as 100 versions at once and get back only what matters per package: how many findings it has, its worst risk level, and the version deps.dev would recommend instead. The one-step audit of a whole lockfile.
get_findings_batch.display_name: Check many versions for safety findings
get_findings_batch.name: get_findings_batch

parameters.description: The registry the package is published to.
parameters.name: system

parameters.description: One 'name@version' entry per package, up to 100. All of them must be from the ecosystem chosen above.
parameters.name: versions

get_package.description: List every version of a package that has been published, newest first, with each one's publication date and whether it is deprecated. The registry's current default version is marked and returned on its own, so this doubles as the 'what is the latest version?' lookup.
get_package.name: get_package

parameters.description: The registry the package is published to.
parameters.name: system

parameters.description: The package's name exactly as its registry spells it. Maven uses 'group:artifact' and Go uses the full module path.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: How many rows to return. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Leave on to list the newest versions first. Turn it off to walk the package's history from its first release forward.
parameters.name: newest_first

get_project.description: Get a source repository's stars, forks, open issues, licence and description, together with its OpenSSF Scorecard - the 0-10 supply-chain health score and every check behind it, from branch protection to dependency pinning. The five lowest-scoring checks are pulled out for you.

project.description: Fast, unopinionated, minimalist web framework for node.

checks.description: Determines if the project is "actively maintained".
checks.name: Maintained
checks.reason: 17 commit(s) and 3 issue activity found in the last 90 days

weakest_checks.description: Determines if the project uses fuzzing tools, e.g. OSS-Fuzz.
weakest_checks.name: Fuzzing

get_project.name: get_project

parameters.description: The source repository, as 'github.com/owner/repo'. GitLab and Bitbucket work the same way, and pasting the repository's URL is fine.
parameters.name: project_id

get_project_package_versions.description: List the package versions that come from a source repository, across every ecosystem. Rows backed by a signed attestation are served first, so this is how you confirm that a package really is built from the repository it claims.
get_project_package_versions.display_name: List packages published from a repository
get_project_package_versions.name: get_project_package_versions

parameters.description: The source repository, as 'github.com/owner/repo'. GitLab and Bitbucket work the same way, and pasting the repository's URL is fine.
parameters.name: project_id

parameters.description: How many rows to return. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

get_projects_batch.description: Look up as many as 100 source repositories in a single request, each with its stars, licence and OpenSSF Scorecard score - the way to rank a shortlist of candidate dependencies on supply-chain health in one step.

project.description: Fast, unopinionated, minimalist web framework for node.

checks.description: Determines if the project is "actively maintained".
checks.name: Maintained
checks.reason: 17 commit(s) and 3 issue activity found in the last 90 days

get_projects_batch.name: get_projects_batch

parameters.description: One repository per entry, as 'github.com/owner/repo', up to 100. Pasted URLs are fine.
parameters.name: project_ids

get_requirements.description: Get the dependency constraints a version declares in its own manifest, before any resolution: the version ranges from a package.json, pom.xml, Cargo.toml, gemspec or go.mod. Each requirement comes back as a name, a constraint and the group it belongs to (runtime, dev, peer, target framework), and the untouched ecosystem-native block is returned alongside.
get_requirements.name: get_requirements

parameters.description: The registry the package is published to.
parameters.name: system

parameters.description: The package's name exactly as its registry spells it. Maven uses 'group:artifact' and Go uses the full module path.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: The version to look at. Leave empty to use the registry's current default (latest) version.
parameters.name: version

get_version.description: Get everything deps.dev knows about one version of a package: its licences, the security advisories that affect it, whether it is deprecated, where its source and issue tracker live, and its Package URL. Leave the version empty to look at the current latest release.
get_version.name: get_version

parameters.description: The registry the package is published to.
parameters.name: system

parameters.description: The package's name exactly as its registry spells it. Maven uses 'group:artifact' and Go uses the full module path.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: The version to look at. Leave empty to use the registry's current default (latest) version.
parameters.name: version

get_versions_batch.description: Look up as many as 100 package versions in a single request - a whole lockfile's licences and advisories in one step instead of one step per package. Versions that deps.dev does not index come back marked as not found rather than failing the step.
get_versions_batch.name: get_versions_batch

parameters.description: The registry the package is published to.
parameters.name: system

parameters.description: One 'name@version' entry per package, up to 100. All of them must be from the ecosystem chosen above.
parameters.name: versions

lookup_purl.description: Look a package or version up from its Package URL (purl) - the identifier CycloneDX and SPDX bills of materials are written in. The way into deps.dev for a workflow that starts from a generated SBOM rather than a name someone typed. A purl with a version answers with that version; one without answers with the package.
lookup_purl.name: lookup_purl

parameters.description: The purl to look up, with or without a version after the '@'.
parameters.name: purl

lookup_purls_batch.description: Resolve as many as 100 Package URLs in a single request - hand it the purl list straight out of a CycloneDX or SPDX bill of materials and get every licence and advisory back in one step. Purls may mix ecosystems freely.
lookup_purls_batch.name: lookup_purls_batch

parameters.description: One purl per entry, up to 100. They do not have to be from the same ecosystem.
parameters.name: purls

description: Check open source dependencies with deps.dev, Google's Open Source Insights service. Look up any package on npm, PyPI, Maven, Go, crates.io, NuGet or RubyGems for its licences, its security advisories and whether it is deprecated; expand a version into the full transitive dependency graph it resolves to; read a repository's OpenSSF Scorecard; check a package for malicious code, deprecation and typosquat neighbours; and audit a whole lockfile or SBOM in one step by name or by Package URL. No account or API key is required.
